_meta.indication: Savella is indicated for the management of fibromyalgia.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm, fixed-dose trial comparing Savella 50 mg BID and 100 mg BID to placebo; six-month duration
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 to 70 years with fibromyalgia by American College of Rheumatology criteria and baseline pain score of at least 50 mm on a 100-mm VAS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite responder analysis (FM Pain and FM Syndrome) requiring >=30% improvement in pain (VAS), PGIC rating of improved, and improvement in function
pivotal_trials.n: At the 3-month landmark (UPA analysis): placebo N=223, 100 mg/d N=224, 200 mg/d N=441
pivotal_trials.result: At the 3-month landmark (UPA analysis, BOCF imputation), Composite Pain Responders: placebo 43 (19%) vs Savella 200 mg/d 118 (27%), odds ratio 1.54 (1.0, 2.3), p=0.0323; Composite Syndrome Responders: placebo 27 (12%) vs 200 mg/d 85 (19%), OR 1.80 (1.1, 2.9), p=0.0175. The six-month results for the 200-mg per day FM pain endpoint were not statistically significant.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm, fixed-dose trial comparing Savella 100 mg/day and 200 mg/day to placebo; three-month duration
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with fibromyalgia (ACR criteria) and baseline pain score of at least 40 mm on a 100-mm VAS and FIQ physical function score >=4
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite FM Pain and FM Syndrome responder rates at the 3-month landmark
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo N=401, 100 mg/d N=399, 200 mg/d N=396
pivotal_trials.result: Composite FM Pain responders at 3 months (BOCF): placebo 66 (16%) vs Savella 100 mg/d 91 (23%), OR 1.50 (1.1, 2.1), p=0.0252, and 200 mg/d 98 (25%), OR 1.68 (1.2, 2.4), p=0.0037. Composite FM Syndrome responders: placebo 35 (9%) vs 100 mg/d 58 (15%), OR 1.79 (1.1, 2.8), p=0.011, and 200 mg/d 55 (14%), OR 1.75 (1.1, 2.8), p=0.015.

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reaction was nausea (37% all Savella vs 20% placebo); other common AEs included headache (18% vs 14%), constipation (16% vs 4%), dizziness (10% vs 6%), hot flush (12% vs 2%), and hyperhidrosis (9% vs 2%). Serious/warning risks include elevated blood pressure and heart rate, seizures, hepatotoxicity (rarely fulminant hepatitis), and the boxed warning for suicidality.
target_moa: Milnacipran is a selective norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake inhibitor that inhibits norepinephrine uptake with greater potency than serotonin; the exact mechanism of its central pain inhibitory action in fibromyalgia is unknown.
modality: Small molecule (selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, SNRI)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SUICIDALITY AND ANTIDEPRESSANT DRUGS — Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies; Savella is not approved for use in pediatric patients.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved, due to known serious class risks of serious psychiatric symptoms including suicidal ideation.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the product was not the first in its class and no major safety concerns were found that would bring into question approvability.

summary.text: Savella (milnacipran HCl) was approved under a traditional (full) approval pathway via NDA 22-256 (section 505(b)) received December 18, 2007 and approved January 2009 for the management of fibromyalgia, based on two Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials; no advisory committee was convened, and the approval included a REMS with a Medication Guide plus PREA pediatric and 505(o) postmarketing study requirements.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received December 18, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Savella (milnacipran HCl) 12.5 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg Tablets.
This new drug application provides for the use of Savella (milnacipran HCl) Tablets for the management of fibromyalgia.

This application was not presented to an advisory committee meeting as the product is not the first in its class and as no major safety concerns were found during our review that would bring into question the approvability of the product based on its risk:benefit profile.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the management of fibromyalgia in pediatric patients ages 13 through 17 (final report due October 2014).

requirement.text: Develop and maintain a prospective, observational pregnancy exposure registry study in the U.S. comparing pregnancy and fetal outcomes of women exposed to Savella during pregnancy to an unexposed control population (required under 505(o)(3)).

citations.quote: Develop and maintain a prospective, observational pregnancy exposure registry study conducted in the United States that compares the pregnancy and fetal outcomes of women exposed to Savella (milnacipran HCl) during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: A single-dose, pharmacokinetic, open-label clinical trial in healthy, lactating women to assess milnacipran concentrations in maternal plasma and breast milk to estimate potential infant exposure (required under 505(o)(3)).

citations.quote: A single-dose, pharmacokinetic, open-label, clinical trial in healthy, lactating women. Concentrations of Savella (Milnacipran HCl) will be assessed in maternal plasma and breast milk so as to estimate potential infant exposure.
